Overview.Description: A high-performance relay server written in Rust that connects 1-4 TF2 game servers using a custom Raw TCP Protocol for maximum efficiency in local infrastructure.

Goals.Goal: Enable real-time cross-server communication between TF2 servers
Minimize latency with raw TCP packets instead of JSON/HTTP
Support 1 to 4 concurrent servers with seamless scaling
Maintain high reliability in local network environments

CrossServerMechanics.Description: This section documents the core mechanics that enable gameplay interactions between players on different servers. The most critical feature is cross-server Medic healing, which requires careful synchronization.

GhostPlayerSystem.Description: To enable cross-server interactions (healing, damage, etc.), each server maintains "ghost" representations of players from other servers. These ghost entities are visible and interactable but exist only as proxies.
GhostPlayerSystem.Concept: A fake player entity created on Server A that represents a real player on Server B. Ghost entities: - Are visible to all players on the local server - Have synchronized position, health, team, and class - Can receive healing, damage, and status effects - Forward all interactions back to the real player's server

Implementation.Step: When a player joins any server, a PLAYER_SYNC event is broadcast to all other connected servers containing: Steam ID, name, team, class, health.
Each receiving server creates a ghost entity (fake client or bot) that represents the remote player. The ghost is assigned to the same team.
Player positions are synchronized at a configurable rate (default: 20Hz) using PLAYER_POSITION events. Ghosts are teleported to match.
When a local player interacts with a ghost (heal, damage, etc.), the interaction is captured and forwarded to the real player's server.
The real player's server applies the effect and sends back a confirmation with the updated state (new health, death, etc.).

Event.name: PLAYER_SYNC
Event.Description: Full player state sync for ghost creation/update

CrossServerHealing.Description: Enables a Medic on Server A to heal a player (ghost) that represents a real player on Server B. The healing effect is applied to the real player on their actual server.

Workflow.name: Medic Heals Remote Player
Workflow.Step: Medic on Server A points Medi Gun at a ghost entity representing Player X from Server B. SourceMod detects healing beam lock.
Plugin hooks OnTakeDamage or custom healing detection to capture: - Healer Steam ID (Medic) - Target Steam ID (ghost's real player ID) - Heal amount per tick - Medi Gun type (for Über build rate)
Server A sends HEAL_REQUEST event to relay with target Steam ID. The ghost receives NO actual healing on Server A (it's just a proxy).
Relay identifies which server owns the target Steam ID and forwards the HEAL_REQUEST to that server (Server B in this case).
Server B receives HEAL_REQUEST, finds the real player, and applies healing using SetEntityHealth or TF2_AddPlayerCondition for overheal.
Server B sends back HEAL_CONFIRM with the player's new health value so Server A can update the ghost's displayed health bar.
Server A receives HEAL_CONFIRM and updates the ghost entity's health display to match the real player.

Event.name: HEAL_REQUEST
Event.Description: Request to heal a remote player

UberChargeMechanics.Description: When a Medic's Über target is a ghost (remote player), the invulnerability effect must be applied on the target's actual server.

Workflow.name: Cross-Server Über
Workflow.Step: Medic activates Über on ghost target
UBER_SHARE event sent with uber_type and duration
Ghost on Medic's server shows Über visual effect
When Über ends, UBER_SHARE with is_active=0 is sent

LatencyConsiderations.Note: Healing must feel responsive. Target latency: less than 50ms round-trip on local infrastructure. If latency exceeds 100ms, consider predictive healing on the Medic's server with reconciliation.
LatencyConsiderations.Strategy: If enabled, Server A optimistically applies healing to the ghost immediately, then reconciles when HEAL_CONFIRM arrives. This makes healing feel instant even with network latency.

CrossServerDamage.Description: Similar to healing, damage dealt to ghost entities is forwarded to the real player's server for application.

Event.name: DAMAGE_REQUEST
Event.Description: Request to damage a remote player

Extension.name: AsyncSocket Extension
Extension.Description: Modern, high-performance socket extension built on libuv (the same async I/O library used by Node.js). Designed specifically for minimal server jitter and maximum efficiency when processing external network packets.

Features.Feature: Built on libuv for maximum async I/O efficiency
Minimal game server jitter when processing packets

Installation.Step: Download asyncsocket.ext.dll (Windows) or asyncsocket.ext.so (Linux) from srcdslab releases

Plugin.name: tf2_relay_client
Plugin.Description: SourceMod plugin that hooks game events and forwards them to the Rust relay server via TCP. Also receives events from other servers through the relay.

RelayServer.Description:
Central relay server written in Rust using async/await with Tokio runtime. Manages connections from all TF2 servers and broadcasts events between them.
Features a Terminal User Interface (TUI) by default for real-time monitoring. CLI mode available with --cli flag for headless/scripted operation.

Modules.Module: Entry point, CLI parsing, and mode selection
Terminal User Interface rendering and input

Arguments.Argument: Run in CLI mode (no TUI). Logs to stdout. Use for headless servers, scripts, or when TUI is not supported.
Log level: trace, debug, info, warn, error.

TUI.Description: Real-time monitoring interface using ratatui. Displays connected servers, live event feed, statistics, and system status. Keyboard-driven navigation.

Layout.Panel: Application title, version, uptime, and current time.
List of connected TF2 servers with: - Server ID and name - Connection status (connected/disconnected) - Current player count - Current map - Last heartbeat time

Live feed of relayed events: - Chat messages with player names and server origin - Player deaths with attacker/victim info - Player connections/disconnections - Round start/end notifications Color-coded by event type and server of origin.
Real-time statistics: - Total events relayed - Events per second - Bytes transferred - Connected servers count - Uptime

SettingsPanel.Description: In-TUI configuration panel accessible via F2. Allows runtime modification of dynamic settings without restarting the relay. Changes are saved to settings.toml automatically.

Configuration.Description:
Configuration is loaded from settings.toml on startup. In TUI mode, dynamic settings can be modified at runtime via the Settings panel (F2). In CLI mode (--cli), all settings are read-only from the file.
Settings are classified as: - STATIC: Can only be changed at startup (requires restart) - DYNAMIC: Can be changed at runtime via TUI

Option.name: bind_address
Option.Description: IP and port to bind the relay server

Option.name: max_servers
Option.Description: Maximum number of TF2 servers (1-4)

Option.name: connection_timeout_ms
Option.Description: Timeout before considering a connection dead

Option.name: heartbeat_interval_ms
Option.Description: Interval between heartbeat packets

Option.name: position_sync_rate_hz
Option.Description: How often to sync ghost positions per second

Option.name: predictive_healing
Option.Description: Enable optimistic healing for lower perceived latency

Option.name: ghost_interpolation
Option.Description: Smooth ghost movement between position updates

Option.name: max_ghost_latency_ms
Option.Description: Maximum acceptable latency for ghost updates

Option.name: level
Option.Description: Log verbosity: trace, debug, info, warn, error

Option.name: file
Option.Description: Optional file path to write logs

Option.name: log_events
Option.Description: Log all relayed events to file/console

Option.name: log_packets
Option.Description: Log raw packet data (debug only, high volume)

Option.name: refresh_rate_ms
Option.Description: UI refresh interval in milliseconds

Option.name: max_event_history
Option.Description: Maximum events to keep in history

Option.name: color_scheme
Option.Description: TUI color theme

Option.name: show_timestamps
Option.Description: Show timestamps in event feed

Option.name: compact_mode
Option.Description: Use compact layout for smaller terminals

Option.name: broadcast_chat
Option.Description: Relay chat messages between servers

Option.name: broadcast_deaths
Option.Description: Relay death events between servers

Option.name: broadcast_connect
Option.Description: Relay player connect/disconnect events

Option.name: enable_cross_healing
Option.Description: Allow Medics to heal players on other servers

Option.name: enable_cross_damage
Option.Description: Allow damage between players on different servers

Configuration.ExampleFile:
# TF2 Server Relay Configuration # Settings marked with [DYNAMIC] can be changed at runtime via TUI (F2)
[server] bind_address = "0.0.0.0:27050" # [STATIC] IP:PORT to listen on max_servers = 4 # [STATIC] Maximum connected servers (1-4) connection_timeout_ms = 5000 # [DYNAMIC] Connection timeout heartbeat_interval_ms = 1000 # [DYNAMIC] Heartbeat interval
[sync] position_sync_rate_hz = 20 # [DYNAMIC] Ghost position updates per second predictive_healing = true # [DYNAMIC] Optimistic healing ghost_interpolation = true # [DYNAMIC] Smooth ghost movement max_ghost_latency_ms = 100 # [DYNAMIC] Max acceptable ghost latency
[logging] level = "info" # [DYNAMIC] trace/debug/info/warn/error file = null # [STATIC] Optional log file path log_events = true # [DYNAMIC] Log relayed events log_packets = false # [DYNAMIC] Log raw packets (debug)
[tui] refresh_rate_ms = 100 # [DYNAMIC] UI refresh rate max_event_history = 1000 # [DYNAMIC] Event history size color_scheme = "default" # [DYNAMIC] default/dark/light/high_contrast show_timestamps = true # [DYNAMIC] Show event timestamps compact_mode = false # [DYNAMIC] Compact layout
[relay] broadcast_chat = true # [DYNAMIC] Relay chat messages broadcast_deaths = true # [DYNAMIC] Relay death events broadcast_connect = true # [DYNAMIC] Relay connect/disconnect enable_cross_healing = true # [DYNAMIC] Cross-server Medic healing enable_cross_damage = true # [DYNAMIC] Cross-server damage

Protocol.name: TF2RelayProtocol
Protocol.Description: Binary protocol optimized for minimal overhead and maximum efficiency. All multi-byte integers use Little-Endian byte order. Strings are length-prefixed with a single byte (max 255 chars).

StringEncoding.Description: Strings are encoded as length-prefixed with a single byte length indicator. Maximum string length is 255 bytes. Strings use UTF-8 encoding.

EventDictionary.Description: Complete dictionary of event types with their packet type IDs and payload structures. Event IDs 0x00-0x0F are reserved for system/control messages. Event IDs 0x10-0x7F are for game events. Event IDs 0x80-0xFF are reserved for future extensions.

Event.name: HANDSHAKE
Event.Description: Initial connection handshake from server to relay

Event.name: SERVER_CONNECT
Event.Description: Notification that a new server connected to the relay

Event.name: SERVER_DISCONNECT
Event.Description: Notification that a server disconnected from the relay

Event.name: ADMIN_MESSAGE
Event.Description: Admin broadcast message (displayed to all players)

EventCategory.name: Gameplay
EventCategory.Description: Core TF2 gameplay mechanics events required for cross-server synchronization in casual game modes. Covers healing, damage, buildings, projectiles, and status effects. All parameters verified from AlliedModders wiki.

Event.name: PLAYER_HEALED
Event.Description: Player receives healing from any source (Medic, Dispenser, health pack)

Field.name: healer_steam_id
Field.description: Steam ID of healer (0 if health pack)

Event.name: UBER_DEPLOYED
Event.Description: Medic activates ÜberCharge on a target

Field.name: medic_steam_id
Field.description: Steam ID of Medic (0 if self-applied)

Event.name: PLAYER_HURT
Event.Description: Player takes damage from any source

Field.name: attacker_steam_id
Field.description: Steam ID of attacker (0 if world)

Event.name: BUILDING_DESTROYED
Event.Description: Building is destroyed by enemy or environment

Event.name: BUILDING_SAPPED
Event.Description: Spy places Sapper on enemy building

Event.name: PROJECTILE_DEFLECTED
Event.Description: Pyro airblasts a projectile or pushes a player

Field.name: weapon_id
Field.description: 0 if pushed player, else projectile weapon ID

Field.name: projectile_id
Field.description: Projectile entity index (0 if player push)

Field.name: pyro_steam_id
Field.description: Steam ID of Pyro who ignited

Event.name: PLAYER_EXTINGUISHED
Event.Description: Player fire is extinguished (water, Medic, Jarate, etc.)

Field.name: healer_steam_id
Field.description: Steam ID of extinguisher (0 if self)

Field.name: thrower_steam_id
Field.description: Steam ID of Sniper who threw

Event.name: SENTRY_ATTACK
Event.Description: Sentry Gun fires at an enemy (for cross-server targeting)

EventCategory.name: Custom
EventCategory.Description: Reserved for custom events that can be defined by server operators. These events have a flexible payload structure with a key-value format.

Optimizations.Optimization: Use bytes crate for zero-copy buffer handling where possible
Non-blocking I/O with Tokio for maximum concurrency
No JSON/text parsing overhead, direct binary field access
